deep.reconstruction:
Context: this is the unpublished continuation of Ramanujan's 'Highly composite numbers' (1915). Here he treats generalized highly composite numbers for sigma_{-s}(N) = sum_{d|N} d^{-s}.

Setting from the previous page. Fix s>0 and a parameter eps>0. For each r>=1, x_r = x_r(eps) is defined by (319):
 x_r^eps = (1 - x_r^{-s(r+1)})/(1 - x_r^{-sr}).
Put phi_r(x) = log[(1-x^{-s(r+1)})/(1-x^{-sr})], so (319) says phi_r(x_r) = eps*log x_r. Also
 Pi_r(x) = prod_{p<=x} (1-p^{-s(r+1)})/(1-p^{-sr}),
so log Pi_r(x) = sum_{p<=x} phi_r(p).
(318) states sigma_{-s}(N) <= N^eps * prod_r Pi_r(x_r) e^{-eps*theta(x_r)} for every N. Equality holds when N = e^{theta(x_1)+theta(x_2)+...}, i.e. N is a 'generalized superior highly composite number' for parameter eps.

§62, transforming the product. Formula (16) is (my inference) the prime-sum partial summation
 sum_{p<=x} phi(p) = pi(x)phi(x) - int pi(t) phi'(t) dt.
With phi = phi_r this gives
 log Pi_r(x_r) = pi(x_r)phi_r(x_r) - int pi d phi_r.
Ramanujan then parametrizes the integration variable along the curve x = x_r(eps). There phi_r = eps*log x, so
 d(phi_r) = log x d eps + eps dx/x.
Hence
 log Pi_r(x_r) = eps*pi(x_r)log x_r - int pi log x d eps - int eps*pi/x dx.

(320). Use theta(x) = pi(x)log x - int^x pi(t)/t dt, i.e. pi log x - theta = int pi/x dx. Then
 log Pi_r(x_r) - eps*theta(x_r) = eps*int pi/x dx - int eps*pi/x dx - int pi log x d eps.
Integration by parts, d(eps*F) = F d eps + eps dF with F = int pi/x dx, turns the first two terms into int F d eps. So the whole equals
 int {F - pi log x} d eps = -int theta(x_r) d eps.
With limits made explicit (mine): as eps -> infinity, x_r -> 1+, so both sides vanish there. Thus
 log Pi_r(x_r(eps)) - eps*theta(x_r(eps)) = int_eps^inf theta(x_r(eta)) d eta.
A direct Stieltjes check (mine): d log Pi_r(x_r) = phi_r(x_r) d pi(x_r) = eps d theta(x_r), so d[LHS] = -theta(x_r) d eps.

(321). Substituting into (318):
 sigma_{-s}(N) <= N^eps exp(-int sum_r theta(x_r) d eps) for all N (and all eps).

(322). The d/d eps of the log of the right side is log N - sum_r theta(x_r(eps)). This is nondecreasing in eps, since each x_r decreases as eps increases. So the bound is minimized when
 log N = theta(x_1)+theta(x_2)+...
This is in the step-function sense, the analogue of §38 for d(N).

(323). Define Sigma_{-s}(N) = Pi_1(x_1)Pi_2(x_2)... with eps tied to N by (322). At that eps the right side of (321) equals Sigma_{-s}(N). The aim is the maximal-order bound sigma_{-s}(N) <= Sigma_{-s}(N), with equality at generalized superior highly composite N. The next page then estimates x_r ~ (r^{1/s}x_1)^{1/r} and Pi_r through zeta(sr)/zeta(s(r+1)).
errors: Integrals are written as indefinite throughout. Limits and constants of integration are suppressed; correctly the identity is log Pi_r(x_r) - eps*theta(x_r) = int_eps^infinity theta(x_r(eta)) d eta. The suppressed boundary terms vanish because x_r -> 1 as eps -> infinity and pi = theta = 0 below 2, so the result is right.

theta and pi are step functions, so (322) cannot generally hold as an exact equation. It must be read as choosing eps where sum theta(x_r(eps)) crosses log N, as in §38. This is not a real error but is unstated.

Formula (16) is invoked without restatement; it is presumably partial summation over primes. The change of integration variable from x to eps along the curve (319) is used tacitly; it is valid because x_r is monotone in eps.

results.what: Identity log Pi_r(x_r) - eps*theta(x_r) = -int theta(x_r) d eps, obtained by partial summation and reparametrizing by eps
results.modern_name: Abel/Stieltjes partial summation; Legendre-transform-type identity in Ramanujan's superior highly composite method
results.usually_credited_to: Ramanujan (unpublished part of 'Highly composite numbers', published 1997 with notes by J.-L. Nicolas and G. Robin)

results.what: Upper bound sigma_{-s}(N) <= N^eps exp(-int sum theta(x_r) d eps), minimized at log N = sum theta(x_r), defining Sigma_{-s}(N) = prod Pi_r(x_r)
results.modern_name: Maximal order of sigma_{-s}(N) via generalized superior highly composite numbers (Lagrange-multiplier / convex duality bound)
results.usually_credited_to: Ramanujan (1915 manuscript, published 1997, Ramanujan J. 1); related work by Alaoglu–Erdős (1944) and Nicolas, Robin

deep.surprise_reason: This page is part of Ramanujan's known unpublished continuation of 'Highly composite numbers', fully published and annotated by Nicolas and Robin in 1997. The manipulations are careful partial summation; nothing here goes beyond what is already attributed to him.

checkable.sympy: from sympy import primepi, primerange, log, Integral; X=50.5; theta=sum(log(p) for p in primerange(2,51)); val=primepi(50)*log(X) - sum(primepi(k)*log((k+1)/k) for k in range(2,50)) - primepi(50)*log(X/50); abs(theta-val)<1e-9
checkable.asserts: theta(x) = pi(x)log x - int_2^x pi(t)/t dt (Abel summation), checked at x=50.5
For r=1, (319) reduces to x_1^eps = 1+x_1^{-s}, i.e. eps = log(1+x_1^{-s})/log x_1 (as used on the next page)
The right side of (319) tends to (r+1)/r as x->1+, so eps -> infinity as x_r -> 1, justifying vanishing boundary terms
eps is decreasing in x_1 (r=1), so x_r(eps) decreases in eps and the minimization in (322) is a genuine minimum
